filename: How Does the Pinatubo Eruption Influence Our Understanding of Long-Term Changes in Ocean Biogeochemistry_.pdf
title: How Does the Pinatubo Eruption Influence Our Understanding of Long-Term Changes in Ocean Biogeochemistry?
code_availability: The CESM source code is freely available from NCAR's Community Earth System Model version 2 (CESM2) (Danabasoglu et al., 2020). The code used to generate the main text figures can be found on Zenodo (Olivarez et al., 2023, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.8145484).
testbed_rationale: The study does not develop, evaluate, or provide data specifically structured for machine learning parameterizations or emulators; it performs climate and ocean biogeochemistry diagnostics using CESM1 large ensembles.
pain_points: Horizontal resolution of the model (~100 km) is coarser than hydrographic measurement spacing (~20 km), requiring spatial aggregation that misses fine-scale structure
Missing volcanic ash micro-nutrients that can stimulate marine ecosystem carbon uptake
Ensemble size limits (29 members) when separating forced signals from high internal variability
extraction_notes: The research focuses purely on Earth System Model ensemble analysis and climate attribution regarding the 1991 Pinatubo eruption's footprint on repeat hydrography biogeochemical indicators. No machine learning techniques are used.
